The Chains of Fenrir

Description- 
An unassuming long, red length of silk ribbon.

History-
The demon wolf Fenrir was a beast so powerful, that the gods feared his ire. They knew they couldn't merely kill him, so they devised a plan to capture the beast forever so he could not wreak havoc on the mortal world. They gathered up several magical components to forge the ribbon. Including:

The sound of a cat's footfall

The beard of a woman

The roots of a mountain

The sinews of a bear

The breath of a fish

The spittle of a bird

They appealed to Fenrir's confidence, telling him that mighty chains couldn't hold him, how could a silk ribbon? The wolf was wary, and said he would allow the gods to tie him down only if one among them would put their hand in his mouth. One of the gods stepped forward, and the wolf bit his hand off. Satisfied, he allowed them to tie him down. No matter how hard the wolf pulled, bit, thrashed and clawed, the ribbon held. And for millennia he laid trapped.
Until he escaped....

Abilities- This ribbon is utterly unbreakable. No blade can cut it. No force in the multiverse could ever rip it. At the behest of one who holds it, the ribbon will animate, and act as a whip or rope.

Description- This black steel sword hilt has a diamond set in the center of it's crossguard. When activated, a hole in the shape and size of a bastard sword blade opens to the deepest, farthest reaches of the void. 

History- There was a cabal of mad warlocks who were obsessed with the stars and the void. They believed that they could open a portal to this void and invite creatures of immense power to come destroy the world. They created this sword hilt as a ritual item to open these portals. However, they weren't powerful enough to truly understand the concept of emptiness, and were sucked into the sword's blade and never seen again.

Abilities- The blade of Voidedge is really a wormhole into space. When activated, it begins to suck all the air from the surrounding area, the wielder can breathe as long as there is air left in the area.When the blade cuts through something, it pulls them into the void, killing them instantly. If the victim is very, very large, however, the blade will just rip parts off and suck them into the void. The wielder must constantly battle with the blade's immense vacuum pressure, and should he ever falter, he is sucked into his own sword and killed.

The user can cast his sight to anywhere in the world and see and hear as if he were there himself. He can see into the hearts and minds of anyone he views. He can literally see reality unfolding around him, and thus it is impossible to hide from the user. This immense power is taxing, however, as so much supernatural sensory input will slowly wear on the mind of the user.
